{{Top}}
{{Youmay|the [[Homing beacon/Legends|homing beacon]], a tracking device|[[Homing Beacon (newsletter)|Homing Beacon]], The Official StarWars.com Newsletter|linebreak=1}}
[[File:Homing_Beacon.jpg|thumb|A homing beacon]]
{{Quote|You're sure the homing beacon is secure aboard their ship? I'm taking an awful risk, Vader. This had better work.|[[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moff]] [[Wilhuff Tarkin/Legends|Wilhuff Tarkin]]|<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref>}}
A '''homing beacon''',<ref name="ANH" /> '''homing device''', '''locator beacon''', '''tracer''', '''tracer beacon''', '''tracking device''', '''tracker''', or '''pulsing beacon''' was used to track [[Starship/Legends|starships]] or any other entity being transported. Capable of transmitting data enormous distances, homing beacons could relay the position of a ship even after several [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] jumps.

==Description==
Homing beacons were small devices that allowed an individual to track a [[Starship/Legends|starship]] across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].<ref name="ANH" /> These devices were advanced versions of [[directional landing beacon]]s&mdash;transmitters that relayed direction and distance information in a series of pulsed transmissions in order to orient starships by providing a fixed reference point for landing.<ref name="A Guide to the SWU">''[[A Guide to the Star Wars Universe]]''</ref> The beacon had an internal [[hyperspace transponder]] which transmits a short-burst, coded [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] signal. The signal was recorded every time it crossed an [[Simu-tunnel/Legends|S-thread]]. Ships traveling through hyperspace crossed at least one S-thread an [[Standard hour/Legends|hour]], allowing a homing beacon to accurately track a target.<ref name="EGWT">''[[The Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology]]''</ref>

S-threads were linked to the [[HoloNet/Legends|HoloNet]], and the beacon's signal was automatically logged and sent to the beacon's control [[Computer/Legends|computer]]. The computer could extrapolate a possible destination from the data, and once the ship dropped out of hyperspace, it broadcast its position with was accurate to within a [[Parsec/Legends|parsec]]. Homing beacons could track a ship's exact movements, which in turn could be used to reveal the position of related locations, such as bases, facilities, or rendezvous points.<ref name="EGWT" />

[[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] beacons used non-mass [[HoloNet/Legends|HoloNet]] transceivers located in hyperspatial "[[Simu-tunnel/Legends|S-threads]]" to track ships through hyperspace. When a homing beacon passed a transceiver, the incident was logged; allowing trackers to determine the heading of a vessel from a collection of these reports.

Many homing beacons were miniaturized, so as to prevent detection by the crew of the ship being tracked. As such, they could be hidden either inside of the ship or tucked in some crevice on the ship's exterior; in fact, some beacon models were small enough to be thrown towards a departing ship's hull.

==History==
[[File:Empire_15_06.jpg|left|thumb|A [[XX-23 S-thread tracker/Legends|XX-23 homing beacon]] aboard the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']]]]
[[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] used such a device on [[Slave I/Legends|''Slave I'']] in order to track [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]] to [[Geonosis/Legends|Geonosis]] just prior to the start of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. Around [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], [[IG-88B/Legends|IG-88B]] used a set of ultra-small microtracers to track [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]], [[Dengar/Legends|Dengar]], [[Bossk/Legends|Bossk]], [[Zuckuss/Legends|Zuckuss]], [[4-LOM/Legends|4-LOM]] and their ships, in an attempt to have them do the work of tracking down [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]] for him.

Grand Master Yoda also used a homing beacon to be tracked by Bail Organa and escape from Palpatine and his shock troopers in Coruscant.

The Empire also used a similar device to track the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']] in order to discover the location of the hidden [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] base on [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]]. The beacon was planted aboard the ''Falcon'' by a [[HMOR homing droid]].

[[Drooim-Durtha Systems]] was a corporation, specializing in the development and manufacturing of tracking devices.

Homing beacons can also be used in an offensive manner, as evidenced by the [[Heinsnake Cult]] using a homing beacon to have [[the basis]] fire an energy ray to obliterate a ''Venator''-class Star Destroyer.
